content: The proposer has indicated that the pesticide in question is registered. Any additional information regarding the active ingredient or its formulation will only be requested from the proposer. A specification will not be published without mutual agreement between the proposer, the Joint Meeting on Pesticide Specifications (JMPS), and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)/World Health Organization (WHO) regarding its content. However, regardless of this agreement, the JMPS evaluation will be made publicly available on the internet by FAO, WHO, or both. The manufacturing process and analytical data concerning the impurity profile of the technical-grade active ingredient (excluding the identity and analytical methods for relevant impurities) are always treated as confidential. In rare cases where information about the ingredients and processes used in preparing formulations is required, this information will also be regarded as confidential. Any previously unpublished information that will appear in the published evaluation is considered confidential until the evaluation is officially published. Unpublished confidential reports or correspondence containing information evaluated by the JMPS will be treated as confidential but will typically be referenced in the evaluation to provide an audit trail for decision-making. A detailed statement outlining the procedures for handling unpublished proprietary pesticide data and addressing potential conflicts of interest in the development of pesticide specifications by the FAO/WHO JMPS is provided in the relevant documentation. The timeline and principles for developing specifications are aligned with the annual FAO/WHO JMPS schedule. For example, in January, FAO and WHO will announce the pesticides to be included in the next three-year JMPS program and the dates of the upcoming JMPS meeting. Before each meeting, FAO and WHO will provide the JMPS with a summary of the requests received. Proposers unable to provide the required data to support a specification must notify FAO and/or WHO as soon as possible to allow adjustments to the program. If a pesticide is withdrawn from the three-year program, an alternative pesticide may be proposed by FAO and WHO. Proposers are expected to submit draft specifications and supporting information to FAO or WHO by September 30. This submission should include one printed copy and an electronic version, using templates available on the FAO and WHO websites. The guidelines provided in the manual must be followed. The proposer must confirm whether their data differ from those submitted to WHO, the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Residues (JMPR), or the registration authorities in the country supporting the FAO/WHO specification. Upon receipt of the draft specification and supporting information, FAO or WHO will assign it to an expert participating in the JMPS for preliminary evaluation. If the toxicological and/or ecotoxicological data provided are identical to those submitted to WHO, JMPR, or the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives (JECFA), their evaluations of hazards and risks will typically be incorporated into the JMPS evaluation. If the impurity, toxicological, and/or ecotoxicological data are identical to those submitted to national authorities for registration purposes, the JMPS will generally interpret this as an indication of the acceptability of the hazards and risks. Registration authorities may be contacted to confirm the similarity of the data, using the proposer’s authorization letter to access proprietary information. If the data submitted to JMPS differ from those evaluated by other organizations, the proposer will be asked to provide an explanation. In cases where no national, JMPR/JECFA, or WHO evaluation is available, FAO/WHO will organize a full assessment of the toxicological and ecotoxicological data before proceeding with the JMPS evaluation. An essential aspect of hazard and risk assessment is determining the relationship between the submitted hazard and purity/impurity profile data and the limits for purity/impurities applied in standard manufacturing production. FAO and WHO recognize that generating duplicate data on all potential or actual hazards by each pesticide manufacturer may be unnecessary and ethically undesirable. However, the absence of direct links between hazard data and manufacturing profiles does not preclude the development or extension of a specification. Proposers will be notified of any additional information required by December 31. They must submit this information to the evaluator and FAO/WHO by February 28 if the proposal and corresponding evaluation are to be considered at the next JMPS meeting. Evaluators should address any questions to the company as soon as they arise to resolve them before the meeting. All communications between the evaluator and proposer related to the proposal under consideration will be copied or reported to FAO/WHO. The evaluator will review the information provided and submit a completed evaluation to FAO/WHO by April 30 for circulation to the proposer and JMPS experts. The evaluation and draft appraisal will also be sent to an assigned peer reviewer by April 30. The peer reviewer does not need access to the original data but should return the reviewed documents to the evaluator and FAO/WHO by mid-May. The peer reviewer will assess the draft specifications, evaluation, and appraisal and provide comments to the author, ensuring consistency with the summarized data and addressing any discrepancies. Proposers who disagree with a draft evaluation or wish to present additional supporting data must provide FAO/WHO with the relevant information at least three weeks before the meeting where the evaluation will be considered. FAO/WHO will forward this information to the evaluator immediately. During JMPS meetings, evaluations will be presented by the evaluator and discussed by the JMPS. If the draft evaluation is disputed or input from the proposer is requested, the proposer may present their case, after which the JMPS will make its final recommendation. Post-meeting amendments involving anticipated responses from the proposer will be accepted for incorporation into the evaluation report. Depending on the number and complexity of minor changes, the JMPS may recommend post-meeting circulation of the final draft evaluation and/or specifications to maintain agreement among experts. Major changes or unexpected and significant new information from the proposer will require reconsideration at a future meeting. If the JMPS cannot reach a consensus, the proposer will be asked to provide additional data to resolve outstanding issues within a specified timeframe. The basis for recommendations to accept or reject specifications will be recorded in the evaluation and cross-referenced with the specifications. Specifications are published on the condition that information on the manufacturing process, impurity profiles, hazard data, and the manufacturer’s name and address remain valid. Proposers are responsible for informing FAO/WHO of any changes to this information. If the validity of this information is in doubt, the specifications may be scheduled for review by the JMPS. FAO and WHO will prepare a program for reviewing all published specifications, which will be considered by the JMPS. Proposers must notify FAO/WHO of changes in the manufacturing process, formulation characteristics, or formulants that could require re-evaluation of the product or review of the specification. Proposals for modifying specifications must be supported by evidence demonstrating that the change is relevant to maintaining or improving the quality, performance, or safety of the technical-grade active ingredient or formulation.
